A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CMoE research despite the changed title. All pages, equations, tables and figures are readable. v1 has no appendices; v2 includes Appendices A–D, which were included in the comparison.

before.justification: Section V reports original language-modeling and downstream-task results, fine-tuning experiments, and expert-activation analyses.

after.justification: Section 4 and Appendices B–C report retained empirical results plus inference speedups, extended fine-tuning, calibration studies and Llama-2 13B experiments.

M1.justification: The ATopK profiling, shared-expert selection, balanced clustering, representative-neuron router, differentiable scaling and load-balancing procedure are retained. The additional experiments apply the existing method; relocating activation analysis to Appendix A does not introduce a component.

E1.justification: v1 uses WikiText-2 for calibration and fine-tuning. v2 adds the diverse SlimPajama corpus for extended fine-tuning and C4 or mixed WikiText-2/C4 calibration. Evaluation retains WikiText-2, C4 and the same six downstream tasks, so coverage expands principally through training and calibration data.

E2.justification: v2 Tables 1–2 add evaluated LLaMA-MoE-v2 comparisons on both base models; v1 only discussed that method. Table 4 also introduces Pythia-1.0B and TinyLlama-1.1B, substantially broadening comparisons beyond the original dense checkpoints and LLaMA-MoE.

E3.justification: v2 introduces FFN and full-model latency measurements in memory-bound and compute-bound regimes, 0.5B/1.2B-token fine-tuning budgets, larger calibration samples and Llama-2 13B experiments. Main baseline and downstream comparisons extend to 75% activation. The original lightweight LoRA settings and downstream shot counts remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendices B–C add calibration-size and calibration-source sensitivity studies, while Section 4.2 investigates extended fine-tuning. v1's fixed-32-expert shared-ratio sweep and detailed activation-ratio curve disappear. Fine-tuning-size and load-balancing analyses are retained; Table 5 redisplays existing configuration results rather than establishing a new ablation.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or run-to-run uncertainty. Results remain point estimates; the retained histogram statistics describe neuron distributions.

E6.justification: v2 adds 75% activation comparison results, inference speedups, small-model and extended-fine-tuning scores, and calibration/13B results. For example, Table 3 reports S1A1E8 full-model speedups of 1.5× and 1.6× in its two regimes. Many 25% results match v1, including values regrouped in Table 5, while other configuration entries and sensitivity results are removed. These additions do not establish same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: v2 Equation 7 explicitly supplies the per-neuron constraint sum_p T_i,p = 1, missing from v1 Equation 11's displayed linear program. The remaining hypotheses and router derivations are retained, largely renumbered or relocated. v1's O(n^3) assignment-solver complexity statement is omitted.

C1.justification: v1 emphasizes rapid carving and inexpensive performance recovery. v2 adds prominent quantitative inference claims: 1.5× speedup at 25% activation and lossless perplexity with 5% acceleration at 75%. The latter strengthens v1's near-dense-perplexity claim into an explicit no-loss claim, although Table 1 still shows perplexity gaps.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive limitations concerning calibration-domain alignment and training-free routing, interprets extended fine-tuning as knowledge transfer and data efficiency, and proposes simpler routing as a configuration advantage. It also adds FFN bottleneck and batch-regime explanations. The earlier interpretation of steadily increasing shared-expert benefits disappears with its sweep.

D1.justification: v2 documents one-epoch SlimPajama fine-tuning with similar LoRA settings and explicitly identifies PPL validation sets. However, it removes v1's NVIDIA H800 PCIe 80GB and CUDA 12.6 information; the new timing study specifies only a single GPU, without batch sizes. Existing calibration, optimizer and LoRA details and code access are retained.

R1.justification: The central positioning as inexpensive dense-to-MoE conversion remains. v2 adds citations to XMoE, Not All Experts Are Equal and SlimPajama, while removing background sources including Balanced K-means, SLEB and the Llama 3 report. The earlier claim of outperforming all cited structured-pruning methods is also removed.

P1.justification: The title changes, and the abstract and introduction are extensively rewritten around inference efficiency. The separate Background section is absorbed into Methodology, activation analysis moves to Appendix A, and the experimental narrative is reorganized into calibration, lightweight fine-tuning and extended fine-tuning discussions.

P2.justification: The document changes from two columns to one, with substantially restructured comparison tables. The overview diagram is relabeled, the two activation histograms are merged into Figure A.1, and load balancing becomes a standalone figure while the other former Figure 5 panels disappear. New speedup, dense-model comparison and calibration tables are added.

improvement.justification: The added baselines, latency measurements and calibration/13B studies address useful gaps in v1. However, v2 loses hardware details and introduces reporting inconsistencies: Table 4's initial CMoE rows combine Llama-2 PIQA/BoolQ values with Llama-3 HellaSwag/Winogrande values from Table 2. Its prominent lossless claim also conflicts with Table 1, including fine-tuned C4 perplexity of 10.21 versus 7.27 for dense Llama-2. Useful additional evidence and limitations coexist with weaker reproducibility and claim accuracy, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
